plain: A man named Danny claims that by shining a laser while on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, he could see a kind of code behind reality. Andrew Gallimore, a neuroscientist, offers another explanation on Jesse Michels's podcast: laser light makes a grainy speckle pattern on the retina, the light-sensing layer at the back of the eye. He says that under DMT the brain uses this pattern like a scaffold and builds complex forms around it, so the code would come from the eye and brain, not from reality itself.
